name: Ironpass MedFront Field Medic Full Rig
description: Olive-drab trauma jacket with reinforced shoulders and a diagonal chest harness loaded with blowout kits, tourniquet loops, and a folded defibrillator patch in sealed pockets over tactical gray cargo trousers. A matte ballistic half-helmet with integrated monocle display tracks patient vitals via BCI relay. Puncture-resistant gloves in dark green nitrile-over-mesh extend to mid-forearm, and waterproof lace-up ankle boots with steel toe protection handle broken urban terrain. The back panel unzips into a flat-fold stretcher.
functionality: Integrated BCI monocle relays patient vitals and triage priority flags; back-panel stretcher deploys in under 20 seconds for solo casualty extraction.
what_it_says: This person runs toward the problem while everyone else runs away, and they've packed every centimeter of kit to prove it.
story_hooks: The monocle display is locked to a frequency that also picks up corporate security comms — someone loaded that firmware deliberately.
The blowout kit contains a sealed vial of an unlisted compound tagged only with a Shelf clinic code.

physical_description.visual_profile: Functional military-medical hybrid silhouette. The wearer reads as a field operative rather than a static medic—broad-shouldered, utilitarian, ready for rapid movement through hostile environments. The diagonal chest harness and visible trauma kit pockets create visual rhythm across the torso. Impression: combat-trained, life-saving capability, zero aesthetic compromise.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through chest and shoulders for layering and movement; tapered at the waist for stabilization. Cargo trousers sit at natural hip with articulated knees. Gloves compress at the wrist. Overall silhouette suggests mobility-first design—nothing restrictive.
physical_description.primary_material: Olive-drab cotton-synthetic blend (trauma jacket), treated ballistic weave panels (shoulders, forearms). Tactical gray recycled composite (cargo trousers). Dark green nitrile-over-mesh (gloves). Matte polymer helmet with reinforced chin strap. Waterproof synthetic leather (boots).
physical_description.texture: Jacket: slightly weathered ripstop with quilted internal padding on shoulders. Harness: coarse webbing with friction-grip surfaces. Trousers: smooth finish with subtle texture at stress points. Gloves: tacky nitrile grip with breathable mesh backing. Helmet: industrial matte finish, zero gloss.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant: muted olive-drab and tactical gray. Accents: dark forest green (gloves), steel gray (helmet visor, boot trim). No bright markings—visibility is irrelevant when your value is measured in lives saved, not spotted.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: heavy-duty YKK zippers (front, back panel zipper for stretcher deployment). Harness: friction-fit quick-release buckles (mag-snap redundancy on critical pouches). Trousers: belted with tactical hook-and-loop. Gloves: elastic wrist cinch. Boots: reinforced lace with speed-lock eyelets.
distinctive_features: Diagonal chest harness with 8 sealed trauma kit pockets (blowout kits, tourniquet loops, defibrillator patch pocket)
Integrated monocle display on matte half-helmet (BCI relay for patient vitals tracking)
Back panel unzips into a flat-fold stretcher (field-deployment critical)
Puncture-resistant reinforced shoulder panels (protection against sharp debris)
Waterproof ankle boots with steel toe cap and textured sole for urban rubble
Internal subcutaneous anchor points on shoulders (for harness compatibility with augmented frames)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary. High-end functional equipment, but not bespoke corpo luxury. Government-subsidized medical apparatus with tactical heritage. Worn by licensed field medics, military corps, and high-risk response teams.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is a life-keeper, not a combatant. Signals: emergency responder authority, trauma expertise, willingness to operate in broken zones. Corpo medical teams, street-level EMT crews with combat training, military field hospitals. The rig broadcasts: 'I know how to stop bleeding, and I've done it under fire.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and field-tested. Jacket shows subtle wear on shoulder seams and lower harness. Gloves are darkened from patient contact (stains that don't wash out). Boots are scuffed. Helmet visor has micro-scratches from dust and proximity. Overall: lived-in, trusted, functional—not showroom-fresh.
